page: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, meaning there is no hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the server includes a bundled 154 GB SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The underlying virtualization is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate that the D4pds_v5 delivers moderate compute capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1822.59, while the multi-core score reached 7252.87, both falling into the average category. However, more complex workloads show some limitations. The Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 1091.0 and 3710.0 are classified as weak, as are the Passmark CPU score of 3157.63 and the Passmark memory score of 1470.18. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, with read speeds at 51.33 GB/sec and write speeds at 30.11 GB/sec, though small block cached reads are weaker at 282.27 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring a poor 651.08, which is likely due to the absence of advanced vector and matrix extensions.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated resource allocation, the D4pds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that do not rely on x86-specific instruction sets or heavy vector mathematics. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, basic database operations (scoring an average 2662.23 in Passmark database tests), and lightweight web serving (achieving 5.45 GB/sec static web serving throughput). It is less suitable for intensive tasks such as large-scale software compilation, complex physics simulations, or large language model inference, where its performance metrics fall into the weak or poor ranges.
description: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v5 is an ARM64-based general-purpose virtual machine from the DPDSv5 family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 154 GB local SSD. Benchmark data shows average performance in stress-ng compute tests and large-block memory bandwidth, alongside average database operations. However, it exhibits weaker results in Geekbench, Passmark CPU, and cryptographic tests, partly due to the lack of advanced vector extensions. This instance provides a qualitatively cost-efficient option for general-purpose workloads, lightweight web serving, and basic database tasks that are optimized for ARM architecture, while being less suited for intensive compilation, cryptography, or machine learning inference.
